info.title: RoofRoof REST API
info.summary: The REST API of a RoofRoof roll-off-roof controller.
info.description:
Every `/api/*` route a RoofRoof roll-off-roof controller serves on port 80. Generated from the firmware's route registry and its contract schemas, so it matches the device.

**The same in every language**: numbers are JSON numbers with `.` as the decimal point, units and field names are never translated, and timestamps are Unix seconds or ISO 8601. Text for people (alert `title` and `message`, `error`) may be reworded between releases: key on the alert `event`, not its text.

**Password**: when protection is on, routes that change something need HTTP Basic auth with the device's username and password.

**ASCOM Alpaca** (`/api/v1/*`, `/management/*`) follows the ASCOM Alpaca standard and isn't repeated here. The device offers two Alpaca devices, the roof as a Dome (`/api/v1/dome/0/*`) and a read-only Switch saying whether the telescope may move (`/api/v1/switch/0/*`); it has no password (the Alpaca design), and its open and close pass the same safety checks as the REST commands. See https://ascom-standards.org/api/.

get.description:
Firmware, memory, flash, time, WiFi (with IPv6 addresses), MQTT, alerts, Alpaca clients and connections. Also pushed over `/ws/status`.

Open: Read-only status for integrations.

503.description: Busy: not enough free memory, try again (Retry-After)

get.description:
Each setting that depends on another, and whether it's in effect or inactive, with the reason.

Open: Read-only effective-settings report (no secrets).

503.description: Busy: not enough free memory, try again (Retry-After)

get.description:
Every setting. Passwords and keys are masked. The `X-Config-Revision` response header carries the settings revision, read before the settings (spec 021): it changes on every save, starts from a random value at each start, and a save can send it back as `baseRevision`. Spec 029: `503` while the device is short of memory (several pages reading at once); nothing is saved, try again.

Open: Read-only, every secret masked.

503.description: Busy: not enough free memory, try again (Retry-After)

post.description:
Partial update: only the fields sent change. A masked or empty password keeps the stored one; `null` clears it. Spec 021: a page sends `baseRevision` (the revision it loaded) and `baseValues` (the values it loaded for the fields it changes). At the current revision the save goes through; at another one, only if each base value still matches the device's (secrets compare masked); otherwise 409 with `conflicts` (the dotted names, at most 16) and `revision`, and nothing is saved. Without `baseRevision` nothing is checked. The answer carries the new `revision`. A wrong value is refused with `error` naming it; a setting whose dependency is off is saved and reported inactive by `/api/settings/effective`. Refused with 409 while the roof is opening or closing or a close is waiting to start (flash writes stall its control task); while the save runs, an open is refused and a close waits for it. Spec 029: `503` while the device is short of memory (several pages reading at once); nothing is saved, try again.

Needs the password when protection is on.

503.description: Busy: not enough free memory, try again (Retry-After)

put.description:
The same as `POST /api/config`, for clients that use PUT, including the `baseRevision` check (spec 021). Refused with 409 while the roof is opening or closing or a close is waiting to start (flash writes stall its control task); while the save runs, an open is refused and a close waits for it.

Needs the password when protection is on.

post.description:
Spec 020: the device fetches the SQMeter's `GET /api/config` (SQMeter sends no CORS headers, so a browser can't) and answers with what the setup wizard and Settings can copy: its location, time zone and NTP servers, MQTT broker, port, user name and base topic, and ntfy server and topic. Each secret (MQTT password, ntfy token, Pushover user key and app token) is only ever reported as set or not: its value never appears, even from an SQMeter that doesn't mask it. Parts an older SQMeter lacks are `null`. Nothing is saved. The address is the body's `url`, else `safety.http.url`, in any form the address setting takes (`192.168.1.50`, `sqmeter.local`, `https://sqmeter.lan`, or a URL ending in one of SQMeter's API paths); only its scheme, host and port are used. https is encrypted without a certificate check. The login sent to SQMeter (HTTP Basic) is the body's `username` and `password` when given (the password mask means the saved one), else the saved `safety.http` login, which only goes to the saved SQMeter's host and port. Refused (409) while the roof moves, a close waits or the automatic close works, and while another copy runs; 502 when SQMeter doesn't answer, wants a password ("SQMeter wants a password"), refuses the one sent ("SQMeter refused the password"), or the reply isn't SQMeter's settings.

Needs the password when protection is on.

address.description: The SQMeter's scheme, host and port, e.g. http://192.168.1.50.

503.description: Busy: not enough free memory, try again (Retry-After)

url.description: SQMeter's address as typed (e.g. 192.168.1.50, sqmeter.local or https://sqmeter.lan). Optional: the saved address when left out.

username.description: SQMeter's user name (HTTP Basic), as typed. Optional: the saved one when left out and the address is the saved SQMeter's host and port.

password.description: SQMeter's password, as typed; the mask (********) or leaving it out means the saved one, which only goes to the saved SQMeter's host and port. Never logged or echoed.

post.description:
Spec 023: starts the wiring check on the device's main loop; read the result with `GET /api/pins/check`. Nothing can move the roof: EN is read for about 50 µs as an input with the internal pull-up while both PWM stay low. Refused (409) while the roof moves, a close waits, the close sequence works, a calibration run or a jog is under way, while the pins in effect are invalid or no board is chosen, while a pin change waits for a restart, and while a check runs.

Needs the password when protection is on.

get.description:
Spec 023: the last wiring check since start-up (`idle` before any): each check's level, reading and text, and `suggestPreset` when the Ethernet probe found a WT32-ETH01 on a board set up without Ethernet. Direction and travel aren't checked (the `motion` item points to the calibration page's jog and teach).

Open: Read-only: the last wiring check's readings and verdicts; no address or secret; changes nothing.

post.description:
Spec 023: the pin rules' errors and warnings for a pin map on this chip, without saving it. A named preset alone fills in its pins; pins sent with a named preset that differ from it are an error. Save a map through `POST /api/config` (`pins`).

Open: Checks a pin map against the pin rules and saves nothing; no address or secret.

get.description:
Spec 023: the pins in effect since the last start (`running`) and as saved, whether a restart is needed to apply the saved ones, whether the pins in effect passed the pin rules at boot (with the reason and every error and warning), whether the chip has PSRAM, the board in effect and, with no board chosen, the board the boot probe found (`detected`; `null` when it didn't run), the presets, and each board's Ethernet and header pins. Read-only.

Open: Read-only: the pins in effect and saved, the rules' report and the presets; no address or secret.

post.description:
Spec 020: the device reads SQMeter's `GET /api/safety` once, as the weather poll does, at the body's address and login (as `POST /api/sqmeter/site` takes them), and answers with SQMeter's verdict. Nothing is saved and the weather source is unchanged. 200 with `safe`, `reasonFlags` and a `text` for people; 502 with `error` when SQMeter doesn't answer ("SQMeter not answering: ..."), wants or refuses a password, or the address answers but not like SQMeter's /api/safety ("That address answered HTTP 404, not like SQMeter's /api/safety", "That address answered, but not like SQMeter's /api/safety (missing safe)"). Refused (409) while the roof moves, a close waits or the automatic close works, and while another read of SQMeter runs.

Needs the password when protection is on.

safe.description: SQMeter's verdict (false whenever it sets a reason flag).

reasons.description: SQMeter's own reasons, joined with "; " (at most 160 bytes; empty when it sent none).

text.description: For people: "SQMeter says safe", or "SQMeter says unsafe: " with SQMeter's reasons, or without them the flags as words ("rain").

post.description:
Spec 027: the device reads N.I.N.A.'s mount information once, as the park check does (Advanced API v2), at the body's `url` (`http://` or `https://`) or, with no body, the saved address. Nothing is saved. 200 with whether N.I.N.A. is `reachable`, the mount `connected`, `atPark` and `slewing`; 502 with `error` when N.I.N.A. doesn't answer ("N.I.N.A. not responding: ...") or answers but not as expected. 400 for a body that isn't `{"url"}` (a string, at most 512 bytes) or an address that doesn't start with http:// or https:// (or none saved); 409 while the roof is busy or another read of N.I.N.A. or SQMeter runs.

Needs the password when protection is on.

post.description:
Asks the roof to open, as a person. Refused unless the weather verdict is safe (constitution III), the mount is confirmed parked (an open needs the park as a close does), the daylight failsafe allows it, and by the motion logic (a latched fault, the Hall reading not settled, the supply low or unreadable, current sense on and unreadable, invalid settings), and with `busy` while an upload or command-line OTA is writing the flash, an MQTT connect is under way or a restart is scheduled. When the park is the only thing refusing it and N.I.N.A. can be asked (an address is set and **Ask N.I.N.A. to park** is on), the open is accepted with 202 and waits: N.I.N.A. is asked to park, and the open runs once the park has held for the park hold time, through every check again; `roof.parkWait` in the status shows the wait, which ends at the park wait limit (`park.timeoutSeconds`, with the critical "mount not parked" alert), on any stop, on a new command, or when another check refuses it (`roof.parkWaitEnded`). When N.I.N.A. can't be asked, the 409 text says so. An optional body `{"override": ["weatherNotSafe", "daylight", "mountNotParked"]}` is the person's confirmed override of those refusals for this open; the weather and daylight overrides stay in effect while the roof opens and end when the roof reads closed, a close is accepted, or a refusal they don't cover (rain, a weather source in doubt, a park switch check) appears. Spec 039 (constitution 10.0.0): `mountNotParked` opens without the park check, at the start and during that one open (the park interlock doesn't stop it), and raises an information alert; the next open checks again. `roof.openOverridable` lists what may be overridden now and `roof.override` what is. A body that isn't JSON of that shape, or names something that can't be overridden, is refused with 400. An accepted open starts after the 500 ms dead time and ends on the open magnet; `GET /api/status` `roof` shows its progress. An open in progress stops if the weather stops being safe (unless overridden) or the park is lost (unless overridden). Refused with `hotspot` while the setup hotspot, which has no password, is on. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

Needs the password when protection is on.

post.description:
Asks the roof to close, as a person. Refused unless the mount is confirmed parked: N.I.N.A. reports it at park and every fitted park switch reads closed (constitution II); refused by the motion logic as for open. When the park is the only thing refusing it and N.I.N.A. can be asked, the close is accepted with 202 and waits for the park as an open does (see `POST /api/roof/open`); when N.I.N.A. can't be asked, the 409 text says so. An optional body `{"override": ["mountNotParked"]}` is the person's confirmed close without the park, for this close only: it isn't re-checked while closing. A bad body is refused with 400. A close in progress stops with a `parkInterlock` fault if the park confirmation is lost. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`. A close always wins: it cancels a scheduled restart and stops an upload in progress (the upload fails with 409). While an upload, another flash write or an MQTT connect is still finishing, the close is accepted with 202 and `pending: true` and starts as soon as it is done (`roof.closePending` in the status).

Needs the password when protection is on.

post.description:
Spec 026: ends a stand-down of the automatic close (`closePhase` `heldByPerson` after a person's Stop, or `halted` after a close that took too long) before its re-arm spell is over, as a person at the roof. Accepted only while the weather check reads safe and daylight doesn't want the roof closed; the next step of the sequence checks again and applies it. It never moves the roof: it arms the automatic close again, so unsafe weather afterwards starts a new attempt. 400 unless `attended` is true; 409 when there is no stand-down or something wants the roof closed. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

Needs the password when protection is on.

403.description: Refused: a required header is missing

attended.description: The person confirms they are at the roof and can see it; must be true.

post.description:
Spec 016: an attended run, started only by a person at the roof. From where the roof is, a slow close to the closed end (unless `at` is `closed`), a slow open and a slow close, and with `topPass` an open and a close at the top duty; each leg stops at the first magnet and is bounded by `roof.calibrationLimitSeconds` (later legs by the measured ones), the existing faults and the drive budget. Refused (409, with `reason` and `error`) unless `attended` is true, the weather is safe, daylight doesn't want the roof closed, the mount is confirmed parked, the automatic close is idle, no fault is latched, the roof is at rest, nothing blocks an open and the Hall reading agrees with `at`. Reasons: `notAttended`, `calibrating`, `closeSequence`, `faultLatched`, `moving`, `closeWaiting`, `settingsPending`, `weatherNotSafe`, `daylight`, `mountNotParked`, `busy`, `hotspot`, `restarting`, `invalid`, `hallDisagrees`, `notStarted`, or the motion logic's (`supplyLow`, `supplyUnreadable`, `currentUnreadable`, `hallNotSettled`, `settingsInvalid`). Read the run with `GET /api/roof/calibration`. Nothing is saved: the proposal is accepted with `POST /api/config`. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

Needs the password when protection is on.

get.description:
Spec 016: the last calibration run since start-up (`idle` before any): its state, the leg under way with its limit, how it ended, each measured leg (time, duty, end level, speed at 100 % duty, current and supply), the Hall readings (in between, and at rest at each end) and, for a finished run, the proposal with the value at the start beside each proposed one (`null` where withheld, with the reason). Read-only, kept in memory only.

post.description:
Spec 019: a person at the roof moves it at the slow duty while they hold a button. Without `id` it starts a jog toward `direction`; with the `id` it answered, it renews that jog. The device stops the jog by itself `holdMs` (500 ms) after the last renewal reached it, by its own control steps, at the first magnet after leaving the one it started on, and after 30 s (or a move from an unknown position's timeout, if shorter) with the `timeout` fault; every motion fault and the drive budget apply. Release with the `id` and `release: true`, which stops that jog only (a person's `POST /api/roof/stop` stops it too). Spec 033: with the Hall rail fault the latched fault (or the Hall reading at a rail or not settled), or with `ignoreMagnets`, the jog runs blind: on time alone at the slow duty, never stopping at a magnet, still only while renewed and at most the jog's limit (not a fault), stopped by a supply-sag stall and every fault still checked; the Hall fault stays latched and the position unknown. A jog toward open needs the weather safe, daylight not wanting the roof closed, the automatic close idle and the mount confirmed parked, and the park interlock watches it. Spec 033: a jog toward closed needs none of these and isn't stopped by them (a close always wins). Start refusals (409): `notAttended`, `calibrating`, `closeSequence`, `faultLatched`, `moving`, `closeWaiting`, `settingsPending`, `weatherNotSafe`, `daylight`, `mountNotParked`, `busy`, `hotspot`, `restarting`, `notStarted`, or the motion logic's (`supplyLow`, `supplyUnreadable`, `currentUnreadable`, `hallNotSettled`, `settingsInvalid`). A renewal or release of a jog that has ended is refused with `jogEnded` and never starts one. While a jog runs, open and close are refused with `jogging`. Needs the header `X-RoofRoof: 1`.

Needs the password when protection is on.

Spec 029: the last 3 unexpected restarts (a crash, a watchdog or a brown-out), newest first, recorded at the start after each one; always on, whatever the diagnostics mode. Needs the password when protection is on (the log lines can name hosts and topics).

Needs the password when protection is on.

Answered from a background task: a second or two with a passphrase. Refusals carry a `code`: 400 `passphrase-short`, 409 `busy` while another backup or preview runs, 413 `too-large`.

Needs the password when protection is on.

Send `""` as the password for an open network. Refused with 409 (with the reason) while the roof is opening or closing, a close is waiting to start, or the automatic close is waiting for the park or closing: it drops the current network for up to 10 s. Until it has joined (at most 15 s), an open is refused and a close waits.

deviceLogin.description: The device's username and password, when protection is on.

roofCommand.name: X-RoofRoof
roofCommand.description: Must be `1`. A cross-site form or simple cross-origin request can't send it, so another site in a browser can't move the roof (403 without it).

source.name: source
source.description: `ui` when the web UI sends it; shown as the reason.

ActionResult.title: Action result
ActionResult.description: What every action endpoint answers on a 2xx status, success true plus details; on a 4xx/5xx status, an error message. Hand-written, not generated: tools/contract-check.py checks the device's actions against it.

Backup.title: Backup
Backup.description: POST /api/backup (src/WebServerBackup.cpp, lib/ConfigBackup): the settings backup file, format 1. Hand-written, not generated.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC; left out when the device clock wasn't set.

settings.description: Every setting as GET /api/config shows it: a set secret is "********", an empty one "".

secrets.description: Only with a passphrase: the eight secrets, encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 key.

data.description: Base64 ciphertext followed by the 16-byte tag; associated data "roofroof-backup/1".

BackupPreview.title: BackupPreview
BackupPreview.description: POST /api/backup/preview (src/WebServerBackup.cpp, lib/ConfigBackup): what restoring a backup would save, before anything is applied. Hand-written, not generated.

token.description: 32 hex characters; send it to POST /api/backup/apply.

backup.description: The file's header, as far as it has one (format 0 is a plain settings export).

settings.description: The settings applying would save, secrets masked as in GET /api/config.

state.description: restored: decrypted with the passphrase; kept: the file has secrets but no passphrase was given; none: the file has none.

changed.description: Secret paths that will change (never values).

notApplicable.description: Settings in the backup this board can't use: not applied, this board's value is kept.

value.description: The backup's value (left out for a secret).

restart.description: Why applying restarts the device; empty: no restart.

baseRevision.description: The X-Config-Revision the sender's copy was read at. When it isn't current, the save goes through only if every value in baseValues still matches the device's; otherwise 409 with conflicts.

baseValues.description: The values the sender loaded for each field it changes (and their credential partners), shaped like the settings; null for a field it didn't have.

heap8Bit.description: Spec 037: the byte-addressable heap malloc and new use (freeHeap and maxAllocHeap also count the IRAM heap).

reserveSpent.description: Spec 038: times the emergency heap reserve was given up so an allocation could succeed, since start.

largestLow15m.description: Spec 045: the lowest largest free block over the last 15 minutes (one reading a second), bytes.

largestLow60m.description: Spec 045: the lowest largest free block over the last 60 minutes (one reading a second), bytes.

blind.description: Spec 030: the move is a blind close (the Hall sensor dead, closing on time alone).

mountMayMove.description: Spec 043: the roof is at rest at its closed or open magnet, so the telescope may slew, park or unpark (the Alpaca Switch "Mount may move").

needsPerson.description: Spec 030: the roof needs a person (a restart with the position unknown, a fault, a Hall sensor failure, the automatic close unable to move), and what for.

weatherHold.description: Spec 030: the automatic close's weather hold: unsafe seconds added up, seconds left before the close is wanted (-1: not counting), whether it has fired.

WifiScan.title: WiFi scan
WifiScan.description: GET /api/wifi/scan (src/WebServerApi.cpp handleWiFiScan). The scan runs in the background: 202 with scanning true and no networks while it runs, then 200 with the list. Hand-written, not generated.
